stem: What is an Import Set in ServiceNow?

options.text: A staging table for raw imported rows.
A snapshot of a database for backup.
A type of UI Action record.
A scheduled job that runs every hour.

rationale: Import Sets are the staging pattern. Raw rows land in a staging table (sys_import_set_row + a per-import schema), then Transform Maps shape and move the data into target tables. Two-step design lets you re-run transforms, debug, and audit.

distractor_notes.D: Schedules can run imports, but an Import Set itself is the staging concept.

stem: What is a Transform Map?

options.text: Maps staging fields to target fields.

rationale: Transform Maps define the field-by-field mapping from staging to target, with optional source scripts to compute target values. Multiple maps can run against the same Import Set (one row → many tables, for example).

stem: On a Transform Map, what does a Field Map define?

options.text: Maps a source field to a target field.
Which records to delete after import.

rationale: Each Field Map is a single source→target field rule. Configure Choice Actions (Reject, Create, etc.), the Coalesce flag (use this field to find existing records to update), and optionally a source script to compute the value.

stem: A nightly import brings 50,000 user records. Some users already exist; the import should update them, not duplicate them. What is the mechanism?

options.text: Set Coalesce = true on the Field Map for the unique key.
Delete the target table before each import.
Run a Business Rule to manually deduplicate after import.

rationale: Coalesce is the upsert mechanism. Mark the unique-identifier field map as Coalesce = true, and the transform does find-or-create per row. Multiple coalesce fields combine as AND.

distractor_notes.B: Truncating before each load destroys history and isn't idempotent.
distractor_notes.C: Post-hoc dedup is bug-prone and wasteful.
distractor_notes.D: Disabling ACLs is a security regression.

stem: What is a Data Source record in the import context?

options.text: A subset of the User table.

rationale: Data Source = where and how to fetch the raw data. The platform pulls per the configuration (or accepts file uploads), and lands rows in the associated Import Set staging table. Then transforms run.

stem: A developer needs to load a one-time CSV of asset records into a custom table. What is the correct platform-supported path?

options.text: Paste the CSV contents into a Business Rule.
Load the data using Import Sets.
Type each row by hand into the table form.
Email the CSV to ServiceNow Support.

rationale: Import Sets are exactly the supported one-time and ongoing load path. Stage → transform → review → repeat. The Transform History gives you per-row success/error visibility.

distractor_notes.C: Manual entry for thousands of rows is impractical.

stem: What do Transform Map scripts (e.g., onBefore, onAfter, onForeignInsert) allow you to do?
rationale: Transform Map scripts are the hooks: onBefore (modify target before insert/update), onAfter (post-transform logic per record), onForeignInsert (handle missing referenced records), onStart/onComplete (per-import boundary work). Powerful — but use only when field maps alone can't do it.

stem: After a nightly import, a developer notices duplicates appearing on the target table. The Field Map has Coalesce = true on employee_number. What's the most likely cause?
rationale: Coalesce is an exact-match query. ' 00123 ' != '123'. Inconsistent source formatting is the classic duplicate-creator. Normalize in the source script (or upstream) so coalesce sees a single canonical value.

stem: Which utility automatically matches source field names in an Import Set to identically-named field names on the target table, creating Field Map records as a starting point?
rationale: Auto Map Matching Fields scaffolds Field Maps where source and target field names match. Saves clicking when your source data has been pre-shaped to match target column names.

distractor_notes.C: CI Relationship Builder is for CMDB graph, not field mapping.
distractor_notes.D: BSM Map is for service-relationship visualization.

stem: An import is finished; the developer wants to verify exactly how many rows were inserted, updated, ignored, or errored. What is the right tool?
rationale: Transform History (sys_import_set_run / Transform History) is the source of truth: counts per outcome and links to per-row results. Always inspect it after meaningful imports.

distractor_notes.C: ACL Debug is for access decisions.

stem: How do you set up an Import Set to run automatically on a schedule (e.g., nightly)?

options.text: A Scheduled Import on the Data Source.
Hard-code the schedule in a Business Rule.
There's no scheduled import; it has to be manual.

rationale: Scheduled Imports attach a cadence to a Data Source. The platform pulls, stages, and transforms on schedule. Each run is logged so you can see results and re-run if needed.

distractor_notes.C: Business Rules don't pull data from external sources.
distractor_notes.D: Scheduled imports are core to the feature.

stem: A developer's import is mapping department_name from CSV to department (a Reference field to cmn_department). Most rows transform fine, but some report an 'unresolvable reference' error. What's likely happening and the right fix?

options.text: Some CSV values don't match a department.

rationale: Reference fields in imports require resolution. Unresolvable means the source string didn't match any target record. Fix the source data, add missing referenced records, or use a Choice Action / onForeignInsert hook to handle it gracefully.

distractor_notes.A: Not broken — your data is mismatched.

stem: What is the Inbound REST API in ServiceNow?

options.text: A built-in set of REST endpoints.
A scheduled job that polls external sites.

rationale: Inbound REST = external callers hitting your instance. The platform provides standard table APIs (/api/now/table/...) and lets you define Scripted REST APIs (/api/{namespace}/...) for custom endpoints. ACLs and authentication apply.

stem: What does Outbound REST allow?

options.text: The platform makes HTTP calls to external APIs.
Browsing the web from the navigator.

rationale: Outbound REST is the instance reaching out. Configure a REST Message (or use Flow's REST Step / IntegrationHub spoke), and the instance calls the external endpoint with auth, headers, params, and body. Results come back into the calling script or flow.

stem: What is SOAP, and how does ServiceNow support it?

options.text: SOAP is a legacy XML-based web services protocol.
SOAP is the platform's encryption library.
SOAP is a type of ACL.

rationale: SOAP is the older XML-based web services protocol. The platform supports it for compatibility with legacy systems, but for new work REST is the modern default. Know SOAP exists; prefer REST.

stem: A developer needs to call an external REST API from a Business Rule. What is the recommended platform pattern?

options.text: Write raw socket code in JavaScript.
Email the API team to do the call manually.
Store credentials in plain text in the script.

rationale: REST Message records separate config (endpoint, auth, default params) from code (which method to call, what to pass). That makes credentials manageable, auth changes safe, and the script readable. Use it.

distractor_notes.B: Not how the platform calls REST.
distractor_notes.D: Plaintext credentials in code is a serious security issue.

stem: Which authentication options are typically available for outbound REST calls from ServiceNow?

options.text: Basic Auth, OAuth 2.0, and API key.
No auth — REST is always anonymous.

rationale: ServiceNow supports the common auth flavors for outbound REST: Basic, OAuth 2.0, mutual TLS, API keys, etc. Use Connection & Credential Aliases to share credentials across multiple REST Messages without duplicating secrets.

distractor_notes.D: SAML is for SSO, not API auth.

stem: What is a Scripted REST API?

options.text: A custom REST endpoint you define.
An old name for the Table API.

rationale: Scripted REST APIs let you expose custom endpoints with arbitrary URL paths and per-method scripts. Use them when the standard Table API would be a clumsy fit — for example, an endpoint that aggregates several tables into a single response.

distractor_notes.B: Table API is built-in and separate.

stem: A developer's outbound REST call is failing intermittently with timeouts. What's the most appropriate next step?

options.text: Run the call from your laptop instead.

rationale: Outbound HTTP logs are the source of truth — status codes, durations, error responses. From there, decide whether to tune the message (timeout, retry), the calling code (resilience), or to coordinate with the external API. Don't fly blind.

distractor_notes.D: Personal laptops aren't a substitute for the platform.

stem: What is a MID Server, and when is it used?

options.text: A Java app inside the network.

rationale: MID Server is the agent-in-the-customer's-network. The cloud instance posts work to it; the MID Server executes locally (where firewalls allow it to reach internal systems) and returns results. That's how integrations to on-prem systems usually work.

stem: A team needs to integrate with an external system that exposes BOTH REST and SOAP endpoints. Which should they prefer for a new ServiceNow integration?

options.text: SOAP — it's more verbose so it's safer.

rationale: When both exist, REST is the modern default for new ServiceNow integrations. Better Flow Designer support, JSON over XML, simpler payloads. SOAP is the answer when the external system only offers SOAP.

distractor_notes.C: Import Sets are file/batch oriented; not the right shape for live API integration.
distractor_notes.D: Building both doubles maintenance for no benefit.

stem: A nightly import takes 6 hours and overlaps the business day. What is generally the right optimization?

options.text: Add more rows to make it run faster by paradox.
Audit the transform: scripts, indexes, and rows returned.
Run it manually on the developer's PDI.
Disable ACLs on the target table.

rationale: Long-running imports usually have inefficient field maps, missing indexes on coalesce fields, or pull more rows than needed. Audit the slow parts, ship deltas instead of full loads where possible, and schedule wisely.

distractor_notes.D: Disabling ACLs introduces a security regression.

stem: A developer exposes a Scripted REST API endpoint that returns Loaner Request data. They want to ensure only their app's external partner can call it. What is the right approach?

options.text: Allow anonymous access — anyone needs to be able to hit it.
Disable the endpoint and tell the partner sorry.

rationale: Authentication + role-gated ACLs are the primary controls. Optionally constrain by source IP if you trust your partner's network controls. Obscurity (long URLs) is not a control.

stem: Which is the built-in REST API for performing CRUD operations on platform tables?

options.text: The Table API — full CRUD via /api/now/table.
There is no built-in API; everything must be a Scripted REST API.

rationale: The Table API is the platform-provided CRUD REST endpoint. /api/now/table/incident does GET/POST/PATCH/DELETE with sysparm_query, sysparm_fields, sysparm_limit, etc. Honors ACLs (so the calling user only sees what they're allowed to). Often the right starting point before writing a custom Scripted REST API.

distractor_notes.B: ACLs aren't called as an API.

stem: A recurring user import keeps creating duplicates instead of updating existing records. What should be set?

options.text: A coalesce field on the field map.
A read ACL on the table.
A UI Policy on the form.

rationale: Marking a unique field (like email) as coalesce tells the transform to update the matching record instead of inserting a new one — eliminating duplicates.

distractor_notes.B: Batch size affects throughput, not duplicate matching.
distractor_notes.C: An ACL controls access, not import matching.
distractor_notes.D: UI Policies act on forms, not server-side imports.
